text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure, lower stroke risk, and protect kidney function in people with type 2 diabetes, as detailed by the Mayo Clinic. While generally well-tolerated, it can cause various side effects ranging from mild and temporary to serious.

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness: Especially when standing up quickly, which often improves as your body adjusts.
Cold-like symptoms: Such as a stuffy nose, sinus pressure, or upper respiratory infections.
Fatigue and weakness: Feeling unusually tired, particularly during the first few weeks of treatment or after a dose increase.
Digestive issues: Mild stomach upset, nausea, or diarrhea.
Pain: Back pain, joint pain, or headaches.

text_blocks.snippet: You can read a complete breakdown of how your body reacts on GoodRx.
Serious Side Effects (Seek Immediate Medical Care)

list.snippet: Severe allergic reactions (Angioedema): Sudden swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing or swallowing.
Dangerously high potassium levels (Hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.
Kidney problems: Sudden changes in how much urine you pass, blood in the urine, or swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet.
Very low blood pressure (Hypotension): Severe dizziness, feeling faint, or fainting.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Safety Warning: Losartan can cause serious harm or death to an unborn baby and must not be taken during pregnancy. Do not stop taking losartan suddenly without talking to your healthcare provider, as stopping abruptly can cause your blood pressure to spike.
